text: 🇲🇽✊ 39 years: 29,000 hospital beds. The next 36 neoliberal years: 4,000. "From 1943 to 1982, 29,000 beds were built in 39 years. Over the next 36 years, only 4,000. Now, in 12 years, we will build 9,000." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 18, 2026 Health spending rises 11% this year. Sheinbaum framed the hospital-bed shortage as the inheritance of the neoliberal era — and the 4T's task to reverse.

🇲🇽🌎 "Everything possible — within our sovereignty, with respect, and for the good of Mexico." "What we are asking is the preservation of the treaty... and that the tariffs on steel, aluminum and automobiles come down, so they stop hurting these sectors of the economy." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 18, 2026 Sheinbaum spoke with President Trump on Wednesday — her 22nd call with him since taking office. Talks continue; no closed deal yet.

🚨🇲🇽 Sheinbaum confirms open differences with Washington over CIA agents operating in Mexico. "In the case of Chihuahua, we've had very significant differences related to the participation of CIA agents in an operation. The Attorney General's Office even opened an investigation into it." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 18, 2026 Mexico's federal prosecutor opened a probe into the CIA's role in an operation in Chihuahua. Sheinbaum said the dispute won't stop federal–state coordination.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico opens its first Center of Excellence in Midwifery — traditional knowledge meets modern medicine. "Traditional knowledge is linked with allopathic medicine, without putting anyone’s life at risk. Often there is knowledge that gynecologists don’t necessarily have." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 18, 2026 Opened in San Miguel de Allende and run entirely by women, the center pairs traditional midwives with doctors under Official Norm 020. Care is free.

🇲🇽🎨 Zero VAT for bookstores: "Access to books and reading is a right." "Publishers got this support over twenty years ago, but not distribution — that created an imbalance. Zero VAT means a benefit of around 200 million pesos a year for the sector." — Claudia Curiel, Culture Secretary, Mañanera, Sept 18, 2026 The 2027 budget proposes zero VAT for bookstores. On Sept 21, a 50-million-peso book purchase opens for Mexican independent publishers to stock public libraries.

🇲🇽✊ "We will never impose a project by force." "Much of the opposition to the aqueduct comes from people displaced when the dam was built, who were never compensated as promised. We won’t impose it by force — the goal is water for León, without taking water from anyone." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 18, 2026 40 community meetings have been held over the Solís–León aqueduct. The government says any project will be decided through dialogue.

🇲🇽🔍 León was the most violent city in the country. Guanajuato’s homicides are down 75%. "León was the most violent city in the country when we arrived. Today there is a very important reduction — and the perception of insecurity has dropped 10 to 15 points." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 18, 2026 Guanajuato averaged 12.7 homicides a day in Feb 2025; the 2026 preliminary figure is 4 a day — on track for the state’s lowest in 8 years.

🇲🇽💵 <u>REMITTANCES UP 3% — BUT A WEAK DOLLAR STEALS THE VALUE</u>

Mexican migrants sent home $5.571 billion in July, up 3% and a sixth straight month of growth, Banxico reports — 13.1 million transfers averaging $426 each. But in real terms remittances fell 6.5%: as El Financiero notes, a weakening US dollar means fewer pesos for every dollar of hard-earned money crossing the border. The families keep sending; it’s Washington’s currency that’s shrinking what arrives.

🇲🇽🗿 <u>62 YEARS OF THE PALACE THAT GUARDS MEXICO’S SOUL</u>

The Museo Nacional de Antropología turns 62 — 42,000 m² and 24 halls built expressly to hold Mexico’s memory, from the Aztec Sun Stone on down. It’s the crown of a country that now runs 1,739 museums, 197 in the capital alone, free for everyone every Sunday and always free for students, seniors and kids. Commissioned by López Mateos and designed by Pedro Ramírez Vázquez, it was built — unlike borrowed colonial palaces — to be a museum: a nation choosing to house its own history.

⚽🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO’S ANTITRUST COP GOES AFTER LIGA MX</u>

Mexico’s antitrust commission (CNA) has opened a formal investigation (IO-001-2026) into Liga MX for scrapping promotion and relegation — permanently locking second-division clubs like Leones Negros and Mineros out of the top flight in a business that moves over 52 billion pesos and 150,000 jobs a year. League boss Francisco Iturbide claims smaller clubs “lack the economic solvency to move up”; regulators can fine the guilty up to 10% of annual revenue. In 2021 the same clubs and the FMF were already fined 177.6 million pesos for collusion.
